borough: London Borough of Barking and Dagenham
decision_conditions: The proposed development, by reason of the poor design of the first-floor side extension, particularly its disjointed roof form and lack of alignment with existing built elements, would result in a fragmented and visually incoherent addition. This would undermine the architectural symmetry of the semi-detached pair and detract from the prevailing character and appearance of the surrounding area. Furthermore, the cumulative bulk, massing and scale of the overall development would appear excessively dominant and visually intrusive within the context of a uniform streetscape, which is characterised by consistent spacing and coherent design. The proposal is therefore considered to constitute overdevelopment of the site and would cause harm to the established character of the area. This is considered to be unacceptable and contrary to:National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF) (MHCLG, December 2024) Policy D4 of the London Plan (March 2021)Policies SP2, DMD1, and DMD5 of the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham’s Local Plan (September 2024)The Residential Extensions and Alterations Supplementary Planning Document (February 2012)

The proposed development fails to demonstrate, through clear and accurate submitted plans, that an adequate amount of usable private external amenity space would be retained. The submitted documentation is inconsistent and lacks sufficient clarity, particularly in relation to the existing garage structure and associated garden layout. In the absence of sufficiently clear and accurate plans, the Local Planning Authority cannot be satisfied that the proposed development safeguards a sufficient proportion of private external amenity space to avoid having a harmful impact on the living conditions of existing or future occupiers, and may prejudice third parties who would otherwise have had the opportunity to comment on the application. As such, the proposal fails to demonstrate compliance with the relevant requirements of the Development Plan. This is unacceptable and contrary to:National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF) (MHCLG, December 2024)Policy D4 of the London Plan (March 2021)Policies SP2 and DMD1 of The London Borough of Barking and Dagenham’s Local Plan (September 2024)The Residential Extensions and Alterations Supplementary Planning Document (February 2012)
description: Construction of a part two storey part single storey rear and side extension including roof extension
